Four Feet On Bisectors

GeometryTrianglesCircles
Game: Drag the corners of a triangle and watch four dots where one corner meets the halfway lines at the other two corners.
How to play: Drag A, B or C, or focus a dot and use the arrow keys. Press Show statement to see the straight line through the dots, or Check the claim when you are ready.
Look for the math

Move any corner of the triangle and the four dots move with it — yet they keep lining up. Here is why that is not a coincidence.

Four bisectors, four feet

At B and C there are two angle bisectors: one inside the triangle and one outside it. They are perpendicular. M and N are the feet of the perpendiculars from A to the inside bisectors; P and Q are the feet on the outside ones. The original Java applet had four checkboxes — names, statement, premise and hint — with names switched on in the copy beside the explanation; the live cut-the-knot page now shows a GeoGebra version instead, so the Java behaviour was recovered from the 2007 archived page and the applet bytecode.

A rectangle at B

Because the two bisectors at B are perpendicular, and AM and AP are perpendicular to them in turn, AMBP is a rectangle. Its diagonals give ∠AMP = ∠ABP. The outside bisector cuts the turn outside B in half, so ∠ABP = (180° - B)/2 = (A + C)/2. The logic test confirms both angles on every triangle it tries.

The cyclic quadrilateral, and a slip on the page

Let I be the incenter. The angles at M and N in ANIM are right angles, so A, N, I, M form a cyclic quadrilateral. That gives ∠AMN = ∠AIN. The article prints ∠AIN = A/2 + B/2, but that is a slip: the true value is A/2 + C/2 = 90° - B/2. The page's version only agrees when B = C; the logic test checks the true value on hundreds of triangles and pins the printed one as false in general.

Why the four feet line up

From the rectangle above, ∠AMN = ∠AMP, so M, N and P share a line; Q joins it by the same argument at C. Another way to see the same thing: A lies on the circle through B, I and the excenter opposite C, so M, N and P are feet on the Simson line of A for that triangle. The test checks this circle and the collinearity independently of the drawing code.

Try Show premise, then pull A far to one side and watch the common line tilt while all four right-angle marks stay right.
